articles.title: Is Islam Makhachev Still the Undisputed Champion? #ufc
articles.description: Is Islam Makhachev still the undisputed UFC champion if an interim champion is crowned? Chael Sonnen raises a question about the UFC's championship system: can a title truly be undisputed when another fighter holds an interim belt in the same division? Chael makes an important distinction. He isn't saying Islam has lost his championship. He's arguing that Islam's status as the *undisputed* champion is now open to debate, because the winner of the interim title fight between Morales and Prates would have a competing claim. Chael also questions why an interim title is being introduced when the situation doesn't appear to involve the usual circumstance of a champion being sidelined by injury. Is this just a matter of terminology, or does an interim belt fundamentally change the meaning of being undisputed? articles.title: Alex Pereira Is NOT a Small Heavyweight
articles.description: Alex Pereira says if heavyweight doesn’t work out, he can go back to 205 because he’s “not a big heavyweight.” I was so surprised by that statement that I questioned whether Pereira had actually said it. My editing team had to send me the proof. Israel Adesanya didn’t like it either. His point was simple: Pereira shouldn’t be making excuses after the Ciryl Gane fight or before he steps in there with Sergei Pavlovich. But there’s another problem—I don’t buy that Pereira is a small heavyweight. He’s taller than most heavyweight champions, has a longer reach than almost all of them and weighs around 240 pounds. If Pereira wins the heavyweight championship, we’ll suddenly be having a very different conversation about where he belongs in the all-time discussion. articles.title: Volkanovski Just Had One of the DUMBEST Ideas I've Ever Heard
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski is one of the greatest fighters ever. I respect the guy tremendously. But he just laid out one of the dumbest ideas I’ve ever heard. Volk has talked about fighting Justin Gaethje and retiring together. He’s talked about moving to 155 to “test himself” against Ilia Topuria. And then he says he’ll vacate the featherweight belt afterward so he doesn’t hold up the division. What are we doing here? If you really want to test yourself at lightweight, there’s a very simple way to do it: drop the belt now and move into the division without a guaranteed title shot. That’s what Ilia did. That’s what Max Holloway did. Going up only when there’s a championship opportunity waiting for you isn’t the same thing. You want to test yourself? Great. Drop the belt and actually do it. articles.title: Islam Makhachev Was Offered Prates… I’m Surprised He Said No
articles.description: Matt Brown and Henry Cejudo both came out in support of Islam Makhachev, but I think they’re arguing against something Islam never actually said. Islam didn’t reject Carlos Prates because he wanted an easier opponent or more time between fights. His issue was the date because of Ramadan. That distinction matters. But there’s a bigger question here. Islam previously told me he wanted two more fights: Michael Morales and Shavkat Rakhmonov. Those are two of the hardest guys he could possibly call out. So I was surprised to hear he was offered Prates. And if Islam believes Morales and Rakhmonov are the harder fights, what exactly is wrong with taking Prates? If the money is the same and you believe he’s the easier opponent, take the fight. That’s your job. articles.title: Islam can NOT be Undisputed Champion…
articles.description: The UFC has announced Carlos Prates vs. Michael Morales for an interim championship while Islam Makhachev remains the undisputed champion—and I have a problem with the terminology. By definition, how can an interim champion exist alongside an undisputed champion? We saw a version of this before with Tom Aspinall and Jon Jones, but Islam’s situation raises a different question. Islam isn’t out because of an injury or illness. If Prates or Morales becomes interim champion, doesn’t that mean Islam’s championship is now disputed? I wouldn’t necessarily have handled the situation differently. But the question remains: Is Islam Makhachev still the undisputed champion? articles.title: Volkanovski vs. Gaethje Is a TERRIBLE Idea
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski has a habit of making his career harder than it needs to be. Instead of chasing the easiest matchup and biggest payday, Volk consistently looks for the guy who has earned the opportunity. But this time, he may have gotten something exactly right. Volkanovski wants to beat Movsar Evloev and then move to 155 for a retirement fight against Justin Gaethje. I initially thought the idea had virtually no chance of happening. Then Volk's camp offered an alternative: if he doesn't get Gaethje, he'll stay at featherweight and defend against Aljamain Sterling. Those are two very different nights of business for the UFC. Whether Volk intended it as leverage or not, he may have just played his strongest card. #UFC #MMA #AlexanderVolkanovski #JustinGaethje #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Does ONE Liver Shot Win a Round?
articles.description: Petr Yan landed the best shot of the third round against Merab Dvalishvili, a body shot that clearly hurt him. But was that one shot enough to win the entire round? That’s what I’m trying to understand. Take that body shot away, and I think Merab clearly won the round on pressure, output, takedowns, and control. All three judges gave the round to Yan. The rules prioritize damage, but what exactly qualifies as damage? Is visibly hurting your opponent enough? Does damage have to leave something we can actually see? I’m not claiming the judges got it wrong. I’m asking how we’re supposed to apply the standard consistently. I had Merab winning three rounds to two. #UFC #MMA #MerabDvalishvili #PetrYan #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: This was NOT Knockout of the Year!
articles.description: MMA Weekly believes a wild regional MMA finish could be the knockout of the year, but Chael Sonnen isn't buying it. Chael asks the obvious question: how can something be knockout of the year if it wasn't even the best knockout of the weekend? articles.title: What It's Like to Be Undefeated for Years #ufc
articles.description: What does losing feel like when you've spent years competing without ever experiencing it yourself? Chael Sonnen shares a fascinating story about being undefeated and not knowing what defeat felt like. People kept asking him about it, so Chael did something unexpected: he reached out to his friend Urijah Faber after Faber had lost a fight to hear what the experience was like. It's a rare glimpse into the mindset of an undefeated fighter — someone who has spent so long winning that losing is something he can only understand through someone else's experience. What does an undefeated record do to a fighter's perspective, and can you truly understand defeat until it happens to you?
